q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. The dose depends on the child's weight — check the packaging or leaflet, or ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3].

Do not give ibuprofen if your child has chickenpox, is dehydrated, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [2].

Keep giving plenty of fluids, and continue breastfeeding as normal if your baby is breastfed [3]. The temperature should go down over 1 to 4 days [3].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the priority is to keep fluids going in so your son does not get dehydrated, according to the SEUP [1]. Wait about 20 minutes after he vomits, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour — and if he keeps it down, you can slowly give it more often [1]. Oral rehydration solutions are made for exactly this and can be bought without a prescription, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Do not use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [1].

Get help if:
- He is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [6]
- He vomits a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without drinking [6]
- The vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [6]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or urinates little [6]
- He has severe belly pain or a headache [6]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the common causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [5]. Watch how well they take it; if they keep it down, you can slowly give it more often [5]. Oral rehydration fluids you can buy over the counter are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can help a little, though they do not replace lost nutrients and minerals, according to the CDC [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5].

Get help if:
- They seem very low in energy or floppy [3]
- They vomit many times or refuse all fluids [3]
- Vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [6]
- You think they are severely dehydrated [2]

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common, and in preschool children the usual cause of night-time cough and wheezing is a viral respiratory infection, according to the SEUP [2].

Keep the room calm and let your child rest propped up a little; if your doctor has already prescribed a reliever inhaler such as salbutamol, the SEUP says the bronchial obstruction typically improves with it [2]. If there is no plan yet, ask your doctor before giving any medicine.

Get help if:
- The chest pulls in, ribs or collarbones show when breathing [5]
- Breathing is faster than normal [5]
- A whistling sound when breathing out [5]
- Blue colour around the lips [5]
- Coughing so much they cannot speak [5]

A cough that comes in fits, ends in a whoop or vomiting, or lasts for weeks should also be checked, according to MedlinePlus [1].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and some symptoms of a cold can last for 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough, which the NHS says can last several weeks or months [4].

Keep him comfortable and offer fluids often. Coughing fits can be triggered by irritants like cold air, smoke or fumes, so keep him away from those [2].

Get medical help if:
- Coughing bouts lasting minutes, worse at night [4]
- A "whoop" sound between coughs [4]
- Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout [4]
- Vomiting after coughing fits [1]
- Turning blue or grey, or pausing in breathing (babies) [1][4]

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with the child eating normally, is not one of the situations the guidance covers — the passages here are about fever, not about a cough on its own. What they do say is that a high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

If a fever does appear, the AEPap advises checking the temperature with a thermometer, in the armpit, and starting with physical measures: removing extra clothing, offering fluids, reducing activity, and a lukewarm bath if the child is comfortable [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen are for the discomfort that comes with fever, not to bring the temperature right down, and paracetamol is the usual first choice [4][5]. The dose depends on the child's weight.

Get help if:
- under 3 months and temperature 38C (100.4 °F) or higher [1]
- 3 to 6 months and temperature 39C (102.2 °F) or higher [1]
- a rash, or a rash that does not fade when pressed [1]
- not wanting to eat, or not their usual self [1]
- a fever lasting 5 days or more [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly and itch a lot are often hives, which in childhood are usually caused by an infection rather than an allergy, according to the SEUP [3]. The spots are raised, red patches that move around — appearing in one area as they fade from another — and hives can usually be treated at home [3][5].

Give paracetamol if there is pain or discomfort, and speak to a pharmacist about an antihistamine for the itching [1]. A cool bath, patting the skin dry without rubbing, loose clothes and a cooling cream or gel from the pharmacy can all help [1]. Do not give ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections, and never give aspirin to a child under 16 [1].

Get help now if:
- swelling around the mouth [5]
- struggling to breathe [5]
- difficulty swallowing [3]

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Itchy red bumps on a toddler's legs are often hives, which the NHS describes as raised, itchy patches or bumps that can appear anywhere on the body [1]. Hives are usually caused by an allergic reaction, and the rash itself is not dangerous [2].

To ease the itching, ask a pharmacist about antihistamine treatment for hives — but tell them your child's age, because this treatment may not be suitable for young children [7]. Keep your child's nails short and their skin cool to reduce scratching.

Get urgent help if:
- lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell [7]
- breathing is fast or struggling, or wheezing [7]
- throat feels tight or swallowing is hard [7]
- skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale [7]
- your child becomes very confused, drowsy or dizzy, or is limp and not responding [7]

If the bumps spread, blister, or your child seems unwell in themselves, see your doctor.

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that don't bother her and keep appearing each morning are most often nappy rash, which is common in babies and can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. It can look like red or raw patches on the bottom or nappy area, or spots, pimples or blisters that may be red or brown [1][2].

Keep the area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change [2].

Get help if:
- The spots spread or get worse despite home care [2]
- The skin becomes scaly, dry or itchy, or she seems uncomfortable or distressed [1][2]
- The bottom becomes raw, painful or blistered [1][2]

If the spots are not in the nappy area, or she has a fever, cough, runny nose or red eyes along with a rash spreading from the head down, that would need to be checked, as measles can cause a red spotty rash that starts on the head and spreads downward, according to the CDC [3].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
A knock on the head is a common injury, usually from a fall, and the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

For the next 24 hours, watch him for signs of something more serious [2]. Let him sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [5]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [5]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [5]. Keep him resting from physical and mental effort for 24 to 48 hours, with no sport and no screens, then return to normal activities gradually [3].

Get help if:
- Intense or worsening headache, or one that does not ease with the usual medicine [3]
- Repeated vomiting [3]
- Confusion or disorientation [3]
- Behaviour changes, or trouble speaking or walking [3]
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [3]

A knock on the head like this is common, and vomiting once afterwards can be one of the usual symptoms, according to the SEUP [7]. If they seem sleepy, confused, dizzy or have a headache, that is also part of the picture the SEUP describes [7].

While you get them seen, keep them with you and do not let them eat or drink in case they need to be examined [7].

The SEUP says to go to the emergency department if the child is under three months, or if the fall was from more than one metre [1]. It also says to seek urgent care if any behaviour or attitude worries you [1].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
At around 6 months, breast milk alone no longer meets a baby's energy and nutrient needs, so complementary foods are needed, according to the WHO [2]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the consistency and variety of foods over time [2]. Offer 2–3 meals a day at this age, and keep breastfeeding on demand alongside them [2].

Introduce one food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most babies can have peanut products at around 6 months; if your baby has severe eczema or an egg allergy, ask your health provider first [1].

Do not give honey before 12 months, cow's milk before 12 months, or unpasteurised drinks and foods [1]. Avoid choking risks like sweets, popcorn, whole nuts and grapes unless cut up [1]. No juice before 1 year [1].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and it is given on demand rather than measured out [2]. If your baby has at least 4–5 breastfeeds a day, no other milk is needed [2]. If they are not breastfed, the right milk after 6 months is follow-on formula [2].

Alongside that, offer water in a cup with meals. The AEP does not set a millilitre amount of water for this age; what it does set is a salt limit, because a baby's kidneys are too immature to handle much salt: under 1 g of salt a day up to 12 months, and no salt added to their food [3]. So keep water plain and modest, offered with meals, and let milk do the rest.

During an illness, increase fluids, including more frequent breastfeeds, and offer soft, favourite foods [1].

Get help if your baby:
- Drinks much less than usual or has fewer wet nappies [1]
- Vomits repeatedly or has diarrhoea [1]
- Is drowsy, floppy or hard to wake [1]

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit and refuse vegetables, and the CDC has tips to help picky eaters try new foods [1]. Keep offering a variety — fruit and vegetables, including bitter ones like broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage, alongside starchy foods, protein and full-fat dairy [2]. Offer vegetables as finger foods at each meal so your baby can feed themselves and learn to chew [2]. Keep offering a food many times without pressure; babies often need to see a new food repeatedly before trying it [1]. Aim for about 3 meals a day plus their usual milk feeds [2]. If your baby is growing well and having plenty of wet nappies, there is usually no need to worry. Talk to your doctor if your baby is losing weight, seems unwell, or is not eating or drinking at all.

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula is no longer needed, according to the NHS. Your daughter can drink pasteurised whole cows' milk as her main drink, and she should be eating 3 meals a day plus 2 healthy snacks [6].

Offer a variety of foods at meals: starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; full-fat dairy such as cheese and yoghurt; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, beans or lentils [6]. Give full-fat dairy products, since children under 2 need the extra vitamins and energy [6].

The WHO recommends breastfeeding up to 2 years or longer, and 3 to 4 meals a day with 1 to 2 snacks for children 9 to 23 months [2].

Ask your doctor or health visitor for advice if you are worried about how much she is eating [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differs from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than the number is whether the poops are soft and the baby is comfortable: constipation is when stools become hard and painful or incomplete, sometimes with fewer poops than usual [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Your baby's doctor will want to check any constipation unless it comes with warning signs [3].

Get help if:
- Bad belly pain, or the baby is very down and crying a lot [3]
- Blood in the stool [3]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down milk [3]

Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
It is common and normal for a 9-month-old to wake at night: night wakings are physiological, and almost 30% of children still wake at night at one year, according to the PUC Chile manual [2]. The usual cause at this age is a sleep habit — if a baby always falls asleep in your arms, on waking they want the same conditions to go back to sleep [2].

What to do now: do not intervene each time, so as not to create a bad sleep habit; the child should settle back to sleep on their own [2]. Keep the room quiet and the bedtime routine consistent [5].

When to get help:
- Waking is accompanied by fever, which can trigger night terrors [1]
- Very little sleep overall, with daytime irritability or poor feeding [6]
- Loud snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep [5]

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on only when he lies down is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus: coughing, especially at night or early in the morning, along with chest tightness, wheezing, tiredness and dark circles under the eyes [5]. The SEUP describes the same thing — children may have a cough, sometimes at night, with a feeling of breathlessness, and you may hear a whistling sound as air leaves the lungs [3].

If you notice him working harder to breathe — the chest and ribs pulling in, breathing faster than normal — that needs medical help [3].

Get help right away if he has severe coughing, serious trouble breathing, or turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [5]. A blue tinge around the lips means the oxygen in the blood is low [3].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using albuterol more often than usual can be a sign the asthma is not fully controlled, and the SEUP says most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators, though symptoms can last up to a week [2].

Keep giving salbutamol through a spacer (with a mask for small children), never straight into the mouth, and avoid smoke, allergens and exercise during the flare-up [2]. If there is no clear improvement, the child needs to be seen at a health centre [6].

Get help if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [6]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs or chest pull in, belly moves a lot [6]
- Inhalations needed every two hours or less [6]

The WHO notes inhalers with steroids reduce inflammation and the risk of severe attacks, so daily treatment matters [5].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be stridor — a high-pitched sound — and it often comes with a barking cough and a hoarse voice, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It is usually caused by a virus and often starts like a cold [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Keep the child calm and comfortable, and offer fluids often. If the noise is coming with a cold and a runny nose, keeping the nose clear helps.

Get help now if:
- Breathing becomes difficult or you can see the ribs pulling in or the chest sinking [1][4]
- The child is drowsy, floppy or very irritable [1][4]
- The child refuses to eat or drink [4]
- The skin looks a bad colour [4]
- You are worried about your child's breathing [3]

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can have several causes, and one of them is asthma: chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply is a common symptom, according to the WHO [1]. Symptoms are often worse at night or during exercise, and can be triggered by colds, dust, smoke, pollen or animal fur [1]. Because symptoms like these can also be caused by other conditions, the WHO says people with them should talk to a healthcare provider [1].

The SEUP advises watching at home for difficulty breathing — ribs showing or the chest sinking in, fast breathing, tiring when walking or running — or chest pain when breathing [2]. It says to go to the emergency department if the child's general state worsens, if they are listless, sleepy or very irritable, or if breathing becomes difficult [2]. The SEUP also lists chest or side pain when breathing as a reason to seek urgent care [5].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. Most febrile seizures do not need treatment, but a child having one for the first time needs to be checked in hospital [6].

If your baby has a seizure now: do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5].

Get help now if your child:
- has a seizure for the first time [2]
- has a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes [2]
- is having difficulty breathing [2]
- has stiffness and twitching on only 1 side of the body [2]
- is more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour after the seizure stops [2]

A high temperature is 38C (100.4 °F) or more, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1].

q: my child has a sore throat and white stuff on the tonsils
text:
A sore throat with white patches on the tonsils is often tonsillitis, a common childhood illness in which the tonsils become red and swollen [1]. The white patches are pus-filled spots, which are one of the more severe symptoms [1].

To help at home: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, and rest [6]. Older children can gargle with warm salty water (half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out — not for young children) [6]. Cool drinks, ice lollies or hard sweets can soothe the throat, but do not give young children anything small and hard to suck because of the risk of choking [6]. A pharmacist can suggest treatments such as lozenges or throat sprays [2].

Get help if:
- Pus-filled spots on the tonsils [2]
- A sore throat so painful it is difficult to eat or drink [2]
- Symptoms not gone within 1 week [2]
- A severe sore throat that quickly gets worse, swelling inside the mouth or throat, difficulty speaking, swallowing, breathing or opening the mouth [3]

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
Sore throats are very common and usually nothing to worry about — they normally get better by themselves within a week, according to the NHS [5]. Most are caused by viruses like a cold or flu [3].

To soothe it: offer plenty of water, cool or soft foods, and rest [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help the pain — check the leaflet or ask a pharmacist first, and never give children aspirin [6][1]. Do not give young children small hard things to suck, like lozenges or hard sweets, because of the risk of choking [5].

See a doctor if:
- Your child is under 5 and needs help for the sore throat [2]
- It does not improve after a week [2]
- A very high temperature, or feeling hot, cold or shivery [2]
- Signs of dehydration — peeing less than usual or dark, strong-smelling pee [2]
- A weakened immune system, such as from diabetes or chemotherapy [2]

Get help immediately if your child has difficulty breathing or cannot swallow, is drooling, or makes a high-pitched sound when breathing [2].

q: should I give my daughter the HPV vaccine
text:
The HPV vaccine helps protect against human papillomavirus (HPV), a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex. Some types of HPV are linked to an increased risk of certain cancers, including cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts, according to the NHS [1].

The vaccine works very well at reducing the risk of getting HPV. Since it has been used, there has been a big drop in young people getting conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2].

The most common side effects are mild and do not last long: swelling or pain where the injection was given, headache, a high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness [5]. Serious side effects such as a severe allergic reaction are very rare, and the person who vaccinates your daughter is trained to deal with them immediately [5].

In the United States, the ages for this vaccine follow the national schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter should have it.

q: my son missed his 4 month vaccines, what do we do now

For a missed 4-month visit, the usual approach is to give the vaccines now rather than restart the schedule, according to the AEP [1]. Premature and at-risk babies should follow the same schedule as other babies, starting at 2 months of chronological age, and delays are common in the first 6 months [1]. The dose is the same as for any baby; there is no reason for a reduced or split dose [1].

What to do now: contact your doctor or clinic and book the earliest appointment to catch up. Bring your child's vaccination record so they can see which doses were given.

When to get help:
- Your child is unwell with a fever or illness today — the visit may need to be moved [1]
- Very premature babies (born at or before 28 weeks) may need breathing monitoring for 48–72 hours after the first dose [4]

The exact ages and doses follow the United States national schedule, so your doctor will say which vaccines are due now.

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
Malaria is a potentially fatal infection spread by mosquito bites, not from person to person, and it is preventable and curable, according to the WHO [1]. Early symptoms are often mild and easy to mistake for other febrile illnesses: fever, headache and chills, usually appearing 10 to 15 days after an infected bite [2]. Because the symptoms are not specific, testing as soon as possible is important [2]. In a child returning from Africa, seek medical care promptly for testing.

Get emergency care quickly if your child has any of these [2]:
- Extreme tiredness or fatigue
- Confusion or reduced awareness
- Seizures
- Difficulty breathing
- Dark or bloody urine, yellow eyes or skin, or unusual bleeding

Early treatment of mild malaria can stop it becoming severe [2]. P. falciparum, the most deadly type and the most common in Africa, can become severe and cause death within 24 hours if untreated [1][2]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

Fever itself is not an illness; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections [1].

Check the thermometer and how you measured it, then take the temperature again. If your child does have a fever, offer plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [1]. If the fever is very high, your doctor may recommend an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen — but never aspirin for a child with fever [1]. Paracetamol is usually the first choice, and ibuprofen can be used too [4].

- Is very sleepy, floppy or hard to wake [4]
- Has trouble breathing [4]

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is very common and usually nothing to worry about — it normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [5]. It is often caused by a virus like a cold or flu [4].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, and rest [5]. Avoid smoky places [5]. She is old enough to gargle with warm, salty water — half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out, not swallow [5].

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text:
It is normal for a 9-month-old not to have teeth yet. The first tooth usually shows between 4 and 8 months, but this varies, and you can care for the mouth and gums before any teeth appear, according to MedlinePlus [4].

Wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal, and start using a soft toothbrush as soon as the first tooth appears [4]. Do not put your baby to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. Ask your health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4].

Once teeth come in, brush them at least twice a day, especially before bed, and take your child to a dentist every 6 months [1].

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school

Children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of chickenpox, according to the CDC [1]. A person with chickenpox can pass it on until all the spots have crusted over, so he can go back once every blister has formed a scab [2].

While he is at home: calamine cream or lotion and oatmeal baths can help with the itching, and acetaminophen can help with the fever [3]. Do not give aspirin — with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [3].

Chickenpox is usually mild and lasts 5 to 10 days [3].

Get help if:

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry and it can hurt to pass [3]. It is common and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

What helps, according to the SEUP: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass; add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables; and do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't hold in the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should not be given without asking your paediatrician [1]. It is not essential that a child poops every day — the rhythm and consistency of stools vary from person to person [1].

See a doctor if, according to the SEUP:
- Severe abdominal pain, or a child who is very down and complaining a lot [1]
- Blood in the stool [1]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [1]
- Pain on passing stool, or anal fissures [2][4]

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
A vomiting illness in a baby usually settles on its own within less than a week, according to the SEUP [4]. Keep breastfeeding — offer the breast normally, and even more often if your baby wants it [3]. Give smaller amounts more frequently to reduce the risk of vomiting [3]. If your baby takes formula or solids, offer small sips of extra water (boiled and cooled if under 6 months), and ask your pharmacist about a rehydration solution for regular small sips [2]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks — they can make vomiting worse [2].

Get help if:
- Vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomiting even with nothing in the stomach [5]
- Vomiting is greenish, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [5]
- Sleepy, floppy, very thirsty, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [5]
- Under 3 months old and has vomited two or more feeds [5]
- Severe tummy pain or headache [5]

If your baby has just had a bath or been wrapped in a blanket, their temperature may read higher for a short time — wait a few minutes and try again [3].

Because your baby is under 3 months old, they need to be seen by a doctor today [2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal on the way, and do not give paracetamol or ibuprofen [2][4].

q: my son passed out after standing in the sun for a long time
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Not responding to stimuli
text:
Fainting (syncope) is a sudden, short loss of consciousness. It usually happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, and standing still for a long time in extreme heat is one of the situations that can bring it on, according to the SEUP [2].

If he is still unwell, lay him down and keep him lying flat, and have him drink more fluids, especially after physical effort or heat [4]. Before a faint he may feel nauseous, see blurry, have belly pain or sweating — knowing these signs can help him avoid another one [3].

Get help if:
- Fainting during exercise or while lying down [2]
- Fainting with chest pain or a racing heartbeat [2]
- Repeated fainting [2]
- Fainting with low blood sugar in a diabetic child [2]

In general, fainting is not caused by serious medical problems and does not need special tests, according to the SEUP [4].

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are most often eczema, also called dermatitis, according to MedlinePlus [2]. It is not contagious, and scratching can make the redness, swelling and itch worse [2].

Keep the skin moist and avoid things that irritate it, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, and stress [2]. Calamine creams and oatmeal baths can help with itching [5].

See your doctor if:
- The itch is intense, especially at night [3]
- You see small bumps or lines on the fingers, wrists or arms [3]
- The skin becomes crusty, scaly or looks infected [3]
- It does not get better within a month [1]

q: my toddler is wheezing after running around outside
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: bronchial obstruction that can be triggered by exercise, colds, allergy or pollution, and in preschool children viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheezing, according to the SEUP [2]. Not every child who wheezes in childhood will have asthma later [2].

What to do now: keep your child calm and upright, and let them rest — symptoms often start after physical effort [7]. If your child has been prescribed a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, this is the medicine that relieves the obstruction; give it as your doctor or the leaflet instructs [2].

Get help now if:
- Chest, ribs or collarbones pulling in when breathing [7]
- Breathing faster than normal [7]
- Blue colour around the lips [7]
- Severe breathlessness, continuous cough or difficulty speaking [7]
- Intense cough, severe breathing problems, or pale or bluish face, lips and nails [4]

These are signs of a severe attack, and medical help should be sought immediately [4].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
text:
A blocked nose and trouble feeding are common with a cold or RSV in babies, and there is a lot you can do at home, according to the NHS [1]. Use saline nose drops from a pharmacy to clear a blocked nose [1], and keep the nose free of mucus with nasal washes [2]. Feed smaller amounts more often rather than one full feed [1][2], and hold your baby semi-upright to help them breathe [2]. Give children's paracetamol or ibuprofen if they have a high temperature and are uncomfortable — check the leaflet first to be sure it suits your child [1]. Keep them away from tobacco smoke, and wash your hands often to avoid passing the virus on [2].

Get help if:
- Breathing is difficult — grunting, long pauses, or the tummy sucking under the ribs [4]
- Lips or skin turn very pale, blue or grey [4]
- Floppy and will not wake or stay awake [4]
- Under 5 with a temperature below 36C [4]

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's natural response to fighting an infection, and most children can be looked after at home while it runs its course [1][2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal, offer plenty of fluids, and check on your baby regularly, including during the night [1]. Keep them at home and don't overdress or sponge them down to cool them [1][4].

Because your baby is under 6 months, a temperature of 38°C needs medical advice — the NHS advises calling for advice if a baby under 3 months has a temperature of 38°C or higher, and for babies of 3 to 6 months at 39°C or higher [4]. So it is worth getting your baby seen today.

Get help urgently if your baby:
- has a rash that does not fade when pressed [4]
- is drowsy and hard to wake [4]
- is breathing fast or having difficulty breathing [4]
- has a stiff neck or is bothered by light [4]
- is not feeding or not responding as usual [4]

Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months, and paracetamol is not for babies under 2 months [4].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and the organisations describe them rather than a nebulizer. Asthma symptoms include coughing, especially at night or early morning, according to MedlinePlus [4]. The NHS says asthma symptoms may be worse at night and early in the morning [6]. Whooping cough also causes coughing bouts that are worse at night, according to the NHS [2].

What to do now: water can help ease a cough, whether your child drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Children under four should not have cough medicine [5].

See a doctor if:
- Your child has asthma symptoms [6]
- Symptoms are waking them at night [6]
- The cough is getting worse or not getting better [3]
- Difficulty breathing, or turning blue or grey [2]
- Severe coughing or serious breathing problems [4]

Whether a nebulizer is needed is a decision your doctor makes.

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण है और यह कुछ दिनों तक रह सकता है, जिससे शरीर में पानी और नमक की कमी हो सकती है [2]। WHO के अनुसार इलाज में ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) का घोल देना शामिल है — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का मिश्रण है [1]। साथ ही ज़िंक की खुराक दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक कम करती है और मल की मात्रा में करीब 30% कमी लाती है [1]। WHO के मुताबिक 10–14 दिन का ज़िंक का कोर्स दस्त की अवधि घटाता है और नतीजे बेहतर करता है [2]।

इनमें स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से मिलें:
- मल में खून आना [1]
- दस्त 14 दिन या उससे ज़्यादा चलना [1][2]
- निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखना [1]
- गंभीर निर्जलीकरण या शॉक [1]

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद निकलते हैं — आमतौर पर बालों की लाइन पर चेहरे से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, हाथ-पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, CDC के अनुसार [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाले दाने हैं, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दानों से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार भी हो सकता है, NHS के अनुसार [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने आते हैं [3]।

दाने दिखने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ, खासकर अगर आपको खसरा या स्कारलेट फीवर का शक हो [1]।

अगर बच्चे के मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। आपके बच्चे की स्थिति को गंभीरता से लेना ज़रूरी है, और ऊपर दिए गए निर्देश के अनुसार आज ही डॉक्टर से मिलना चाहिए।

जब तक आप डॉक्टर के पास पहुँचें, SEUP के अनुसार बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराते रहें [1]। ठोस आहार दे रहे हों तो थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें, ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो [1]।

SEUP के अनुसार इन चीज़ों से बचें: ज़्यादा चिकनाई वाले खाने, मिठाइयाँ और जूस, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक — इनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]। दूध या डेयरी उत्पाद बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं है [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, कुछ भी न पचा पाए, या बिना कुछ पिए भी उल्टी करे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास ले जाएँ [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत ध्यान देना ज़रूरी है। SEUP के अनुसार, अगर बच्चा उल्टी करे या उसका व्यवहार चिंता की बात लगे, तो आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए [1]। अगर गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई हो, तो भी डॉक्टर से जाँच करानी चाहिए [1]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उसके व्यवहार पर नज़र रखें। SEUP के अनुसार, डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि अतिरिक्त परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

अगर बच्चा बेहोश हो, बहुत नींद में लगे, बार-बार उल्टी करे, या उसका व्यवहार सामान्य न लगे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ में पॉटी करते समय बच्चे का रोना आम बात है — रोना बच्चे का तरीका है बताने का कि उसे आराम या देखभाल चाहिए, और कब्ज़ उन कारणों में से एक है जिनसे बच्चा रोता है [2]।

अभी: बच्चे को गोद में लेकर शांत करने की कोशिश करें और रोना कम होने का इंतज़ार करें [1]। भूख, गीला नैपी, गैस, थकान, ठंड या गर्मी जैसे आम कारण देख लें [3]।

मदद कब लें:
- रोना लगातार हो और शांत ही न हो, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा न लगे [4]
- तेज़ बुखार, या दूध/खाना लेना बंद कर दे [4]
- पेट का दर्द बढ़े, उल्टी हो या मल में खून आए [6]
- रोने के बीच बच्चा सामान्य न लगे, पीला पड़ जाए, पसीना आए या सुस्त हो जाए [6]
- 8 घंटे से पेशाब न हुई हो [4]

अगर समझ न आए कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।
sources: [1] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby
[2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[3] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Soothing a crying baby", p. 1 — https:
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथ-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा लाल-नीला पैटर्न दिख सकता है। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल हो जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है — यह सब सामान्य है, SEUP के अनुसार [1]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 2 से 4 दिन रहता है, और यह अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं है [2]। बुखार की दवा देने पर भी तापमान पूरी तरह न उतरे, यह आम बात है और इससे ज़्यादा खतरे का पता नहीं चलता [2]। बच्चे को ढेर सारे तरल पदार्थ पिलाते रहें ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [3]।

इन बातों पर ध्यान दें और डॉक्टर से मिलें:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [5]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [5]
- त्वचा पर ऐसे दाने जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें [5]
- कुछ भी खाना-पीना न ले पाए [5]
- 2 महीने से छोटा बच्चा हो या रोग-प्रतिरोधक क्षमता कम हो [5]
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁL ES LA EVOLUCIÓN ESPERA
[3] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html
[5] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना निमोनिया में गंभीरता का संकेत है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपनी गोद में या खाट पर लिटाकर रखें और उसकी साँसों की गति गिनें — छह महीने से कम उम्र में 60 से अधिक, छह महीने से दो साल में 50 से अधिक, और दो साल से ऊपर 40 से अधिक साँस प्रति मिनट तेज श्वसन माना जाता है [3]। बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]।

खतरे के लक्षण, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]:
- बुखार से दौरे पड़ना
- खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से इनकार
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना
- सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज
- त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में तुरंत इलाज की ज़रूरत होती है [1]। जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) पिलाते रहें [1]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — जितना वह खा सके, सामान्य भोजन छोटी-छोटी मात्रा में और बार-बार दें [1]। स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ बच्चे को सामान्य से भी अधिक बार स्तनपान कराए [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में खुद उतर जाता है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [3]। बुखार शरीर का संक्रमण से लड़ने का स्वाभाविक तरीका है [2]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र में एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन को बारी-बारी न दें, जब तक डॉक्टर या नर्स न कहें [2]। 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या डिहाइड्रेशन वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है।

डॉक्टर को तुरंत दिखाएँ अगर: बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [1]; साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो [1]; कुछ भी मुँह से न ले पाए [1]; गर्दन अकड़ जाए, रोशनी से तकलीफ हो, या दौरा पड़े [2]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN
[2] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://w

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein madad karta hai, aur aap ise dawa ki dukaan se le sakte hain [4]. Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ke liye, AEPap kehta hai ki paracetamol har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Iski matra bacche ke wazan se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi — isliye apne bacche ka wazan jaan lijiye [2][3]. Aap PediBot ke dose calculator se sahi matra nikaal sakte hain [3].

Ibuprofen bhi bukhar kam karta hai aur har 6-8 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, lekin AEPap kehta hai ki shuru paracetamol se karein [2][3].

Turant madad lijiye agar:
- Bukhar 3 din se zyada rahe [3]
- Bacche ko bahut takleef ho ya sust lage [3]
- Dauron (convulsions) aayein [3]
- Saans lene mein dikkat ho [3]

Agar aapne zyada paracetamol de diya ho, to turant medical salah lijiye [7].

text:
Raat ko khansi hona asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ke lakshan hain: seene mein jakadan, khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi khansi, saans lene mein dikkat, jaldi saans lena, thakan, aankhon ke neeche kaale ghere, chidchidapan, aur saans chhodte waqt seeti jaisi awaaz [3]. SEUP ke mutabik khansi raat ko ho sakti hai, saath mein saans ki kami aur ghabrahat bhi ho sakti hai [2].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa saaf rakhein, saans lene mein madad ke liye saline nasal drops istemal kar sakte hain [5]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein, kyunki bachchon ke liye kuch khansi-cold ki dawaiyan theek nahi hoti [5].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein sakht dikkat ya tez saans [3]

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Red, itchy spots on the feet can be heat rash, according to the NHS — small raised spots with an itchy, prickly feeling, often on skin that has been hot or sweaty [4][6]. It is uncomfortable but usually harmless and gets better on its own in a few days [6].

What helps now: keep the skin cool — loose cotton clothes, lightweight bedding, cool baths, and plenty of fluids [4][6]. To calm the itching, put something cold (a damp cloth or an ice pack wrapped in a tea towel) on the spots for up to 20 minutes, and pat rather than scratch [4][6]. Avoid perfumed shower gels or creams [4].

Get help if:
- swelling around the mouth, or trouble breathing [5]
- the rash spreads or does not settle after a few days [6]
- you are not sure what the rash is [6]

text:
बच्चे का सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी करना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत ध्यान देने की ज़रूरत होती है। SEUP के मुताबिक, सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना चिंता का विषय है और ऐसे में बच्चे को तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास ले जाना चाहिए [1]।

जब तक आप मदद पा रहे हैं, बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उसके व्यवहार पर नज़र रखें। अगर बच्चा सुस्त, नींद में, या सामान्य से अलग लगे, तो यह गंभीर हो सकता है [1]।

SEUP के अनुसार, इन स्थितियों में तुरंत आपातकालीन सेवा में जाना चाहिए:
- बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है [1]
- गिरावट 1 मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है [1]
- बच्चे का व्यवहार या हालत चिंताजनक लगे [1]

अगर बच्चा बार-बार उल्टी कर रहा है, उल्टी में हरा रंग, खून, या कॉफी जैसा पदार्थ है, या बच्चा बहुत प्यासा, आँखें धँसी हुई, बिना आँसू रो रहा हो या कम पेशाब कर रहा हो, तो यह भी गंभीर संकेत हैं [3]।

Bacche ka kabz aur potty ke waqt rona aam baat hai, lekin ise theek karne ke liye kuch karna zaroori hai. NHS ke mutabik, kabz un kai kaaranon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bacche rote hain [3].

Aise bachche ko shaant rakhein, seedha litayein aur khilane-pilane mein madad karein; thoda-thoda doodh ya paani baar-baar dein [5].

Dhyan dein aur turant madad lein agar:

SEUP bhi kehta hai ki atyadhik sust hona ya bachche ko jagane mein dikkat hona ek warning sign hai [4].

Agar bachchi ko saans lene mein dikkat ho, hont ya chehra neela dikhe, ya sharir thanda lage, to turant madad lein [3][4].

Tez saans lena bronchiolitis, RSV ya pneumonia jaisi saans ki bimariyon ka lakshan ho sakta hai — NHS ke mutabik, bronchiolitis mein shuru mein zukaam jaisa lakshan hota hai, phir bachcha tez saans lene lagta hai [3]. WHO kehta hai ki 5 saal se chhote bachchon mein khansi ya saans lene mein takleef ke saath tez saans (taquipnea) ya seene ka neeche ka hissa andar dhasna pneumonia ka sanket hai [6].

Ab jo karna hai: bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, aur agar wo doodh ya paani le raha hai to thoda-thoda karke dete rahein — NHS ke mutabik jo bachche theek se doodh nahi le paate unhein jaldi dekha jaana chahiye [3]. Aap jaise ja rahe hain, saans par nazar rakhein.

- Saans lene mein rukawat, hont ya chehra neela ya grey [3]
- Pasliyan andar ki taraf khinch rahi hain [3]
- Doodh ya khaana bilkul band [3]
- Bahut sust, uthne mein takleef [3]

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in whooping cough and croup, according to the NHS [2][5]. In whooping cough, coughing bouts are worse at night and can last for several weeks or months [2]. Croup symptoms are also often worse at night [5].

Keep your child calm and upright during coughing bouts, and offer small sips of fluid often. Do not give honey if your child is under 12 months old.

Get help if:
- The cough is getting worse [4]
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- Breathing is hard or shallow [4]
- Chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- Seizures (fits) [4]

If your child has a barking cough like a seal, a hoarse voice, or a high-pitched sound when breathing in, that may be croup — ask your doctor, who may give medicine to shorten the illness [5].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and the pattern matters. In measles, the rash usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days to the torso, arms, legs and feet, according to the WHO [4]. Chickenpox causes an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back before spreading, according to MedlinePlus [5].

Keep your child comfortable and hydrated, and do not give aspirin if you think it is chickenpox — it can cause Reye syndrome [5]. Calamine creams and oatmeal baths can help with itching [5].

Get medical help if you notice:
- Fever with the rash [4]
- Trouble breathing or severe respiratory problems [4]
- Signs of dehydration from diarrhoea [4]
- Confusion, drowsiness or a seizure [4]
- An ear infection [4]

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It's natural to worry if your child refuses to eat sometimes, but it's perfectly normal for toddlers to refuse to eat or even taste new foods, according to the NHS [5]. Don't worry about what your child eats in a day or if they don't eat everything at mealtimes — it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week [5]. If your child is active and gaining weight, and seems well, then they're getting enough to eat [5]. As long as they eat some food from the 4 main food groups, you don't need to worry [5]. Keep offering a variety of foods and try again another time — children's tastes change [5]. Give small portions and praise them for eating, even if they only eat a little [2]. If they reject the food, don't force them — just take it away without saying anything and stay calm [2]. Don't give too many snacks between meals — 2 healthy snacks a day is plenty [2].

Get help if:
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [1]

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise

text:
For a 6-month-old with a congested chest and a whistling sound, this is often bronchiolitis, which usually starts like a cold with a cough and a blocked nose, according to the SEUP [6]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [3].

Keep feeding them little and often, and watch their nappies: a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or feeding much less than normal, needs urgent advice [3].

Get help now if:
- Breathing gets harder — grunting, tummy sucking under the ribs, or breathing quickly [3]
- Pauses in their breathing [3]
- Skin, tongue or lips turn blue or grey [3]
- They are floppy and will not wake or stay awake [3]
- They seem very tired, irritable or not themselves [3]

Trust your own judgement if your child seems seriously unwell [3].

text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में अपने आप उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें [3]। निर्जलीकरण के संकेत देखें [3]। बच्चा खाना चाहे तो दें [3]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से जाँचते रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा उसके लिए ठीक है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें अगर वज़न 5 किलो से कम हो, चिकनपॉक्स हो या निर्जलीकरण हो [2]। एस्पिरिन 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चों को न दें [2]।

मदद कब लें:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [2]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [2]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]
- खाना न चाहे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे और आपको चिंता हो [2]
- निर्जलीकरण — कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [2]

चिंता हो या दवा से फ़ायदा न दिखे तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [3]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार में बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करके ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें — यह शरीर की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखें, ऐसा विकासपीडिया बताता है [3]। पैरासिटामोल बुखार के लिए दी जा सकती है [3]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- खाने से मना करे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [7]
- पेशाब कम आए, आँखें धँसी हों, रोने पर आँसू न आएँ [7]

तुरंत मदद लें अगर गर्दन अकड़ जाए, दाने दबाने पर न मिटें, दौरा पड़े, होंठ या त्वचा नीली-भूरी दिखे, बच्चा सुस्त हो और जगाने पर न जागे, या साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो [7]।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोन्कियल ट्यूबों में रुकावट से होती है, जिसे घरघराहट कहते हैं, और यह ब्रोन्कोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक हो सकती है, एसईयूपी के अनुसार [2]। छोटे बच्चों में इसका सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल बीमारी है [2]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को सीधा बैठाएँ और शांत रखें, और बार-बार थोड़ा-थोड़ा पानी पिलाते रहें। सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो तो बिना देर किए डॉक्टर के पास जाएँ, एनएचएस के अनुसार [3]।

मदद कब लें:
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ [3]
- खांसी बढ़ती जाए या ठीक न हो [3]
- बुखार, नाक बहना और खांसी के साथ सांस तेज़ चले [3]
- बच्चा दूध या खाना न ले रहा हो [3]
- चेहरे, होंठ या नाखूनों का रंग पीला या नीला दिखे [7]

अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा हो तो अस्पताल भेजा जा सकता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [3]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल, खुजली वाले दाने कई कारणों से हो सकते हैं। छोटे-छोटे बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने उन नन्हीं माइट्स से हो सकते हैं जो त्वचा में घुस जाती हैं (स्केबीज़); उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी लकीरें दिख सकती हैं, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]। स्केबीज़ में खुजली इलाज के बाद भी कुछ हफ्तों तक बनी रह सकती है [1]।

घर पर: ठंडे पानी से नहाएँ और त्वचा को थपथपाकर सुखाएँ, रगड़ें नहीं; ढीले कपड़े पहनाएँ; नाखून काटें और रात में हाथों में मोज़े पहनाएँ ताकि बच्चा खुजला न सके; खुजली के लिए फार्मासिस्ट से एंटीहिस्टामिन के बारे में पूछें [5]। खुजली शांत करने के लिए ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, और खुजाने की जगह दानों को थपथपाएँ [6]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें यदि:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का संदेह हो [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]
- घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, फिर भी ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो सकता है [5]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इस बात का संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [5]।

भारत में टीके राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के तहत दिए जाते हैं, और उम्र तथा खुराक भारत के राष्ट्रीय शेड्यूल के अनुसार तय होती हैं [5]। अपने बच्चे को टीका लगवाने के समय और किस उम्र में कौन-सा टीका देना है, इसकी जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से लें [3]।

टीके समय पर लगवाना सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा के लिए ज़रूरी है; अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाएँ [3]। टीके सुरक्षित, असरदार हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं [3]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — bachchon mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai, aur kabhi-kabhi yeh sirf khansi se shuru hota hai [5][7]. SEUP ke mutabik khansi ke saath saans phoolna, seene ka dhadakna ya seeti ki awaaz bhi ho sakti hai [1].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa saaf rakhein aur bachche ko aaram karne dein [4]. Agar khansi ke saath zukaam ya bukhar ho, to SEUP kehta hai ki bahut saara paani aur taral cheezein dein [6]. Kisi bhi dawa ke baare mein apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein — bachchon ko aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein takleef ya tez saans [4]
- Hoth ya chehra neela ya peela pad jaye [5][7]
- Bahut bechain ya sust ho jaye [7]
- Seene ki pasliyan andar dhas rahi hon [7]
- Khansi ke saath bukhar 4 din se zyada rahe [4]

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur inhe dekhkar hi pata chalta hai ki kaun sa hai. WHO ke mutabik khaaj (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas kar raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [2]. Chhote bachchon mein yeh rash zyada gambhir ho sakta hai, khaas kar hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par [2]. MedlinePlus ke mutabik eczema mein twacha sookhi ho jaati hai aur khujli hoti hai, aur rash kohni ke andar, ghutnon ke peeche, chehre, haathon aur pairon par ho sakta hai [6].

Agar saans phoolne lage, hoth, muh, gala ya jeebh achanak soojh jaaye, twacha neeli, grey ya pale ho jaaye, bachcha sust ya jawab na de, ya behosh ho aur uth na sake, to turant madad lein [7].

Yeh jaankari sirf aam jaankari hai; apne doctor se mil kar sahi kaaran aur ilaaj jaanch karwaayein.

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai. WHO ke mutabiq, bachchon ko difteria ke saath polio se bachav ki inactivated vaccine bhi combination mein di jaati hai, aur sabhi bachchon ka poora primary vaccination aur teen booster doses zaroori hain taaki lambi avadhi tak suraksha mile [6]. Spain ke vaccination schedule mein bhi polio (VPI) shamil hai, jahan yeh 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein DTPa ke saath di jaati hai [3].

Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to bina der kiye apne doctor se milein aur pending doses poore karwayein. Vaccination ko lekar koi bhi sawaal ho to apne doctor ya local health worker se baat karein.

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea after travel is usually an infection of the gut caught from contaminated food or water, and the main danger is dehydration, according to the WHO [6]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [5]। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने पर इंजेक्शन की जगह दर्द, सूजन और थोड़ी लाली भी हो सकती है [5]। खसरे का टीका लगने के 6-7 दिन बाद हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं; इनका इलाज ज़रूरी नहीं, ये अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

टीके के एक-दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक इंजेक्शन देने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह के अनुसार ही दें [5]। बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के हिसाब से खुराक तय होती है।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बुखार या लक्षण 2-3 दिन में ठीक न हों [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

टीकाकरण की उम्र और खुराक भारत की राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण तालिका के अनुसार तय होती हैं।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body can't cool itself, usually after too long in the heat or sun, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Dizziness is one of the signs to take seriously: with heat stroke, get medical help right away [3].

What to do now: move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to lower their temperature, according to the SEUP [6].

Get help if:
- Fever above 39°C that won't come down with home measures [7]
- Loss of consciousness or seizures [7]
- Confusion, trouble speaking or moving [7]
- Persistent vomiting, can't keep fluids down [7]

Do not use fever medicines for heat stroke — use physical cooling measures instead, according to the AEPap [5].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Solid khana shuru karne ka behtareen waqt tab hai jab bacha taqreeban 6 mahine ka ho, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Is se pehle sirf doodh (breast milk ya first infant formula) bache ki tamam energy aur nutrients pura karta hai [4].

Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke bacha kitna khata hai — asal maqsad usay khane ki aadat dalna hai; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh se hi milte hain [2]. Doodh ke saath saath mukhtalif qism ke khane dene se bacha aage behtar khane ka aadi ban sakta hai [2]. Aahista aahista miqdar aur variety barhate jayein yahan tak ke bacha ghar ke baqi logon ka khana chhote hisson mein kha sake [2].

Agar bacha waqt se pehle paida hua ho, to solid khana shuru karne ke waqt ke bare mein apne doctor ya health visitor se poochein [2].

Choking se bachne ke liye: 5 saal se chhote bachon ko sabut nuts na dein; weaning shuru karte waqt nuts ko pees kar ya grind kar ke khane mein mila sakte hain, aur peanut butter toast par laga kar de sakte hain — akela nut butter na dein [5]. Agar khandan mein allergy ki history ho to koi bhi nut dene se pehle doctor se baat karein [5].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose, watery stools like this are usually gastroenteritis, an infection of the gut that causes more frequent, softer stools, sometimes with tummy pain, vomiting or fever, according to the SEUP [2].

The most important thing now is to prevent dehydration. Give an oral rehydration solution — a mix of clean water, salt and sugar in the right proportions — in small amounts often, after each loose stool or vomit [2][5]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks, and do not give medicine for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [1]. Keep offering food; there is no need to fast, just smaller amounts more often, and avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices [6]. Sports drinks should be avoided [6].

See a doctor if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [1]
- Vomiting a lot, or not keeping down solids or liquids [6]

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe and effective, according to the NHS. Protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [2].

The ages at which it is given follow India's national immunisation schedule, so check the timing with your doctor.

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text:
It is not possible to tell from scratching alone what is causing the bumps. Scabies causes intense itching, often worse at night, with bumps and itchy lines between the fingers, on the wrists, arms, legs and around the waist, according to the WHO [1]. In babies and young children the rash can be more widespread, affecting the palms, soles and sometimes the scalp [1].

Eczema is another cause: it makes skin dry and itchy, with a rash on the face, inside the elbows, behind the knees, and on the hands and feet, and scratching can redden the skin and increase the swelling and itch, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Eczema is not contagious [2].

See your doctor so the cause can be identified, since scabies is diagnosed by recognising its typical features [3].

Check the temperature with a digital thermometer under the arm, and offer plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [1][3]. - is not eating, not themselves, or showing signs of dehydration [7]

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time

At around 6 months, your baby still gets most energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula, and solid foods are introduced alongside it [1]. Start with small amounts — just a few pieces or teaspoons of food — at a time when you are not rushed and your baby is not too tired, offering food before their usual milk feed [1]. Offer a variety and keep offering foods even if rejected; it can take 10 tries or more before a new food is accepted [1]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at this age, increasing amounts gradually [3]. q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools several times a day is diarrhoea, and the weakness you are seeing is often from the water and salts lost in the stools, according to the WHO [4]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — which replace the water and electrolytes lost in the faeces [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key treatment: they shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [2].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [2]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [2]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [2]
- Refusing to eat or drink [2]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [2]

A baby who is passing less urine than usual may be dehydrated. q: my 6 month old has started eating food, what should I give first

q: how do I know if my child is dehydrated from diarrhoea
text:
Signs of dehydration include being very thirsty, crying without tears, passing little urine, or sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness are also signs [2].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — in small amounts, and keep offering nutrient-rich foods and breast milk during the episode, according to the WHO [1]. Zinc supplements shorten the episode and reduce stool volume [1].

Get help if:
- Very thirsty, no tears, little urine, sunken eyes [2]
- Drowsy, irritable or less responsive [2]
- Cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid [2]
- Refuses to eat or drink [2]
- Persistent or severe tummy pain, or a lot of blood in the stool [2]

The risk of dehydration is greater the younger the child [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your doctor [2].

q: when to start feeding puree to 6 months old

From around 6 months of age you can start giving your baby solid foods, beginning with puréed or blended foods if you like, according to the NHS [2]. Some babies prefer to start with mashed, lumpy or finger foods instead, and either way is fine [1][2].

q: is 6 in 1 vaccine safe for my baby

The 6-in-1 vaccine is given as part of your baby's routine schedule, and the ingredients in vaccines are used in very small amounts with no evidence they are harmful at those levels, according to the NHS [1]. Aluminium salts, the most common adjuvant, have been used safely in routine infant vaccines for more than 70 years, and no harmful effects have been seen with vaccines containing them [1].

Serious allergic reactions to any vaccine are rare, and if they happen they usually start within minutes, while the person vaccinating your child is trained to treat them immediately [7].

- You are worried about your baby having a vaccine [7]
- You are not sure whether your baby can have a vaccine [7]

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text:
Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts (ORS) to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and the stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

No se puede saber con esta información qué causa el sarpullido: la urticaria son placas rojas y elevadas que pican mucho y, en la infancia, la mayoría están ocasionadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. El eccema también causa sequedad, comezón y sarpullido, y rascarse enrojece la piel y aumenta la picazón, según MedlinePlus [1].

Mientras tanto, evite lo que irrita la piel, como ciertos jabones, telas y lociones, y las cosas que le causan alergia, como ciertos alimentos, el polen y los animales [1].

Busque ayuda si:
- Le cuesta respirar o tragar [3].
- Se le hinchan las manos, los pies, los codos o la cara [3].
- El sarpullido no mejora o empeora [1].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es la inflamación de la capa externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y en la mayoría de los casos se cura sin tratamiento médico, según MedlinePlus [1]. Para los párpados pegados al despertar, lava los párpados con agua limpia: hierve el agua, déjala enfriar y limpia con suavidad las pestañas con un algodón limpio para quitar las costras, usando uno distinto para cada ojo [3]. También puedes poner un paño frío sobre los ojos unos minutos para aliviar la molestia [3]. Si no estás segura de que sea conjuntivitis, consulta a tu médico.

Busca ayuda si:
- Dolor en los ojos [2]
- Sensibilidad a la luz [2]
- Cambios en la visión, como líneas onduladas o destellos [2]
- Ojos muy rojos [2]
- Un bebé de menos de 30 días con ojos rojos y pegajosos [2]

Si los síntomas no han mejorado en 7 días, consulta a tu médico [2].

Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño tranquilo y en una posición cómoda, y no le des jarabes ni medicamentos para la tos sin consultar [7].

- Se pone morado o pálido [5]

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre y rigidez en el cuello
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Rigidez de nuca: hay que descartar una meningitis ahora mismo
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día. En un niño mayor, la fiebre es una señal de que el cuerpo se está defendiendo de una infección, según MedlinePlus [2].

La rigidez de cuello es uno de los signos por los que hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato, junto con fiebre alta repentina, dolor de cabeza intenso y náuseas o vómitos [1]. Mientras llega la ayuda, asegúrate de que esté bien hidratado, en una habitación a temperatura neutra y sin sobreabrigarlo, según la SEUP [5]. No lo bañes en agua fría ni le pongas paños húmedos, porque resulta desagradable y no es eficaz [5].

Vigila su estado general y que tenga buen color, y la aparición de puntos rojos en la piel que no desaparecen al apretarlos [4].

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Su hija ha sufrido un golpe en la cabeza, que es lo que los médicos llaman traumatismo craneal y suele ocurrir por una caída [1]. Los síntomas más habituales son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia [1].

Mientras la llevan a que la vean hoy, permanezcan a su lado y no la dejen sola. Aunque la exploración médica no muestre alteraciones, se recomienda reposo físico y mental entre 24 y 48 horas, sin deportes ni pantallas, y reincorporarse después de forma gradual [6].

Vigilen y comuniquen de inmediato si aparece alguno de estos signos, según la SEUP [6]:
- Dolor de cabeza intenso, progresivo o que no mejora con paracetamol o ibuprofeno.
- Vómitos repetidos.
- Desorientación o confusión; en niños muy pequeños, irritabilidad o dificultad para despertarlos.
- Cambios en el comportamiento, dificultad para hablar o caminar.
- Sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos.

Según MedlinePlus, busque ayuda de inmediato también si hay convulsiones, incapacidad para levantarse, pupilas dilatadas, debilidad en brazos o piernas o falta de coordinación [4].

Si tu hijo tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de vacunarse es un efecto esperado y pasajero: la vacunación puede empeorar de forma transitoria el curso clínico, aunque estas situaciones son poco frecuentes, según el CAV-AEP [1]. q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
Es normal que a los 9 meses todavía no le hayan salido los dientes: la mayoría empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, pero algunos bebés empiezan antes de los 4 meses y otros después de los 12 meses, según el NHS [1]. Los primeros suelen ser los incisivos centrales, hacia los 6 meses, y los laterales, hacia los 8 [4].

Mientras tanto, cuida sus encías: límpialas al menos dos veces al día, sobre todo antes de dormir, según MedlinePlus [3]. Cuando asome el primer diente, empieza a cepillarlo dos veces al día unos 2 minutos con pasta fluorada infantil (mínimo 1.000 ppm) y solo una pizca, según el NHS [6].

Conviene que lo vea un dentista cada 6 meses [3]. Consulta si a los 12 meses sigue sin ningún diente, o si notas encías muy rojas, hinchadas o que le duelen [1].

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text:
Perder palabras que antes decía es una señal para actuar pronto, según los CDC: si tu hija ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, no esperes [3].

Lo que puedes hacer ahora:
- Habla con el médico de tu hija, cuéntale tu preocupación y pide una evaluación del desarrollo [3].
- La Academia Americana de Pediatría recomienda cribado del desarrollo con herramientas validadas a los 9, 18 y 30 meses, y de autismo a los 18 y 24 meses, o siempre que un padre o el profesional tenga una preocupación [3].
- Si tú o el médico seguís preocupados, pide derivación a un especialista que la evalúe más a fondo [3].
- Pregunta por el programa de intervención temprana de tu zona para saber si puede recibir servicios de ayuda [3].

Cuanto antes empiecen los servicios de desarrollo, mejor es el resultado; entre ellos están la terapia del habla, la fisioterapia y el preescolar de desarrollo [5]. Tú conoces mejor que nadie a tu hija: no esperes [3].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas distintas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón, según el NHS [1]. No te autodiagnostiques: si te preocupa, consulta a tu médico [1].

Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo puede ser un esguince o una contractura muscular [1]. En un adolescente activo, el dolor muscular tras el deporte es una causa posible [1].

Conviene consultar al médico si el dolor va y viene, o si se va rápido pero sigue preocupando [7].

Busca ayuda médica inmediata si el dolor:
- No desaparece, o se siente como presión u opresión en el pecho [7].
- Se extiende al brazo, el cuello, la mandíbula, el estómago o la espalda [7].
- Se acompaña de sudoración, náuseas, mareo o falta de aire [7].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y en general ocurre cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños suelen recuperarse rápido, en un par de minutos [5].

Mientras se recupera: si empieza a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato, y que respire lenta y profundamente [5]. Si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado para que respire mejor [5]. Cuando el malestar haya pasado, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5].

Conviene consultar en urgencias si:
- Tarda más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento [3].
- El desmayo ocurre haciendo ejercicio o esfuerzo [3].
- Se acompaña de palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho [3].
- Hubo sacudidas de brazos o piernas, o se orinó sin querer [3].

Para prevenirlo, que beba más líquidos, sobre todo al hacer ejercicio [4].
